title: FPU Capability Probe
description: Three simulated chips probed with the same MVFR0 bit-field check, showing the register value, the AND mask isolating the low nibble, and the resulting verdict.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Computer Architecture
Embedded Systems
chapter_title: Does Your CPU Have an FPU?

learningObjectives: Apply the MVFR0 bit-field check to determine FPU presence
Demonstrate that one function gives correct answers on different hardware
Explain why a compile-time constant is unsafe

controls.label: Run has_single_precision_fpu()
controls.purpose: Animate the mask and reveal the verdict

simulationModel.modelType: Bit-field extraction against simulated register values
assumptions: MVFR0 values are representative of each core family
Only the A_SIMD field in bits [3:0] is examined
limitations: Real capability detection may also check double-precision and DSP-extension fields elsewhere in MVFR0 and MVFR1

keyQuestions: Why test != 0 rather than == a specific value?
What breaks if this is replaced by a compile-time constant?
commonMisconceptions: That FPU presence can be assumed from the board name
That missing an FPU causes a visible error rather than silent slowness
assessmentOpportunities: Diagnose an unexpectedly slow FFT on an unfamiliar board
